annotation_description: Playing Watery Grave on turn 1 when there's nothing to cast. Either pays 2 life unnecessarily for an untapped land with no use, or enters it tapped and misses the surveil 1 from Undercity Sewers. The hand wants to cast Overlord of the Balemurk (impending {1}{B}) on turn 2, which works fine with a tapped land turn 1 followed by an untapped land turn 2.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: On turn 2, GPT4om Timmy chose to cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its full cost of {3}{B}{B} (5 mana) when they only have 2 lands on the battlefield (Watery Grave and Gloomlake Verge). This spell cannot be cast for 5 mana on turn 2. Even if somehow allowed by the engine, the Impending cost of {1}{B} (2 mana) was the correct and intended line — it gets the enchantment onto the battlefield on turn 2, and it will become a 5/5 creature in 5 turns. Choosing the full cost is either impossible to pay (making this a wasted action) or forces the player to not actually resolve it. The Impending cost is the entire reason you'd play this card early.

Playing a basic Island on turn 2 instead of a tapped dual land wastes an opportunity. With only 1 land in play (presumably from turn 1), playing a tapped land like Meticulous Archive now would let it enter untapped-equivalent by turn 3 while also providing a surveil trigger. The Island provides no extra value. Since the player has No More Lies (WU) and Three Steps Ahead (U) as potential turn 2-3 plays, they want WU available on turn 3. Playing Meticulous Archive (Plains/Island) tapped now gives access to W and U on turn 3 alongside turn 1's land, enabling No More Lies. Playing Island now means they'd need to play Hallowed Fountain (paying 2 life) or another dual untapped on turn 3 to have WU available. Meticulous Archive also provides a surveil to potentially set up draws.

GPT4om Timmy cast Overlord of the Balemurk (for its impending cost of {1}{B}, using 2 mana) before playing a land for the turn. They have three lands in hand (Hedge Maze, Gloomlake Verge, Undercity Sewers) and only two lands on the battlefield. Playing a land first is strictly better - it costs nothing and develops mana for future turns. Additionally, casting Overlord for its impending cost means it enters as a non-creature enchantment with 5 time counters, so it won't be a creature for 5 turns. More importantly, the opponent has only 1 Island untapped and could potentially have interaction. But the real issue is sequencing: land should always be played before spending mana when there's no reason to hold it. Furthermore, the opponent (Libby) has The Unagi of Kyoshi Island in the graveyard, and the Overlord's ETB mills 4 cards and lets you return a non-Avatar creature. However, since it was cast for its impending cost, the 'enters' trigger still fires - it mills 4 and potentially returns a creature from graveyard to hand. Actually wait - let me reconsider. With impending, the permanent still enters the battlefield, so the 'whenever this permanent enters' trigger does fire. So casting Overlord for {1}{B} is a reasonable play to start the impending clock and get the mill+recursion trigger. But the sequencing is still wrong - they should play a land first, then cast Overlord. Playing Hedge Maze (tapped) or Undercity Sewers (tapped) would develop mana without affecting the ability to cast Overlord this turn.

message: You may choose an alternative cost
annotation_description: GPT4om Timmy chose to cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its full cost of {3}{B}{B} (5 mana) when they only have 2 lands on the battlefield (Watery Grave and Gloomlake Verge). They cannot pay {3}{B}{B} with only 2 mana available. Meanwhile, the Impending cost of {1}{B} is exactly 2 mana, which they can pay right now. Even if the game system somehow allows this cast, paying 5 mana when you have 2 lands is impossible, and choosing the full cost over Impending on turn 3 with only 2 lands is a massive mistake. The Impending version gets the enchantment onto the battlefield immediately, starts milling and recurring creatures, and will become a 5/5 creature in 5 turns. Casting at full cost for {3}{B}{B} would require waiting until turn 5+ anyway, so there's no tempo advantage to choosing the full cost - you'd just be delaying the card's impact.

Playing Hedge Maze (enters tapped) instead of Gloomlake Verge (enters untapped) means missing the opportunity to cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost {1}{B} this turn. With Gloomlake Verge, they'd have 3 mana available (Watery Grave + 2x Gloomlake Verge) and could deploy the Overlord immediately, starting the 5-turn countdown on turn 3. The Overlord also mills 4 and returns a creature/planeswalker on entry, potentially recovering The Unagi from the opponent's graveyard via Ardyn later.

GPT4om Timmy cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost ({1}{B}) before playing a land this turn. They have both Gloomlake Verge and Undercity Sewers in hand. Playing a land first (Undercity Sewers, which enters tapped and provides surveil 1) would have been free value — the surveil helps set up future draws and the land would be ready to use next turn. Playing Overlord first doesn't change what they can cast this turn (they have 3 lands and Overlord's impending cost is {1}{B}), but they miss the opportunity to surveil before making other decisions and they risk forgetting the land drop. More importantly, with Undercity Sewers entering tapped anyway, there's no downside to playing it first. The land should always be played before casting spells when it enters tapped with a beneficial ETB trigger.

Grok4F Libby declined to counter Overlord of the Balemurk, a 5/5 that immediately mills 4 cards and returns a creature or planeswalker from graveyard to hand. The opponent already has Deceit in graveyard and could recover it or find other threats. Overlord as an enchantment creature is very difficult to remove and will generate recurring value every time it attacks. Libby has No More Lies available (W+U, which she can pay with Island + Hallowed Fountain) and Three Steps Ahead (counter mode costs 1UU, which she can't pay with only 2 lands). No More Lies would counter it unless opponent pays 3, and opponent has exactly 3 lands - but they're tapped out (they just cast Overlord for 3BB using all 3 lands plus impending cost of 1B). Wait - Overlord costs {3}{B}{B} normally or impending {1}{B}. With 3 lands (Watery Grave, Gloomlake Verge, Hedge Maze), the opponent could cast it for impending {1}{B} (2 mana). That means opponent has 1 mana remaining and couldn't pay the {3} for No More Lies. So No More Lies would have effectively hard-countered the Overlord, and it would be exiled rather than going to graveyard. Letting this resolve gives the opponent a powerful engine that will grind out card advantage every turn.

Casting a spell from hand when the correct play is to pass and hold up No More Lies (W/U) with the two untapped lands. The opponent has a threatening graveyard (Bringer of the Last Gift, Harvester of Misery, Deceit) and 4 lands, meaning they could cast a significant threat next turn. Seam Rip has no valid nonland permanent target on the opponent's board, so it accomplishes nothing. Tapping mana for a useless spell removes the ability to counter the opponent's next play.

GPT4om Timmy cast Overlord of the Balemurk for its impending cost ({1}{B}) before playing a land for the turn. They have Undercity Sewers and Overgrown Tomb in hand. Playing Overgrown Tomb (paying 2 life for untapped) first would give access to 5 mana sources, allowing them to cast Overlord at full cost ({3}{B}{B}) as a 5/5 creature immediately rather than waiting 5 turns for time counters to tick down. Alternatively, even casting it for impending is fine, but they should play the land first to keep options open. Additionally, Superior Spider-Man copying Harvester of Misery or Bringer of the Last Gift from the graveyard could have been a stronger play with the right mana sequencing.

Opponent's Overlord of the Balemurk (likely cast for impending {1}{B}) will trigger on entering, milling 4 cards and returning a powerful creature like Bringer of the Last Gift or Deceit from graveyard to hand. This gives the opponent significant card advantage and sets up devastating future plays. Libby has two No More Lies in hand and can afford to spend one here.

message: Select up to one non-Avatar creature card or a planeswalker card from your graveyard
annotation_description: Overlord of the Balemurk's trigger lets GPT4om Timmy return a non-Avatar creature or planeswalker from their graveyard to hand. The graveyard contains Harvester of Misery, Deceit, and Bringer of the Last Gift among others. Formidable Speaker is not even in the graveyard — it appears as a choice likely from some other zone interaction, but regardless, choosing a 2/4 creature tutor over powerful options like Bringer of the Last Gift (6/6 flying with a devastating ETB that wipes the board and reanimates your graveyard), Harvester of Misery (5/4 menace with -2/-2 ETB), or Deceit (5/5 with hand disruption/bounce) is a significant misplay. Bringer of the Last Gift in particular would be a game-winning threat that synergizes perfectly with the full graveyard GPT4om Timmy has been building. Even Harvester of Misery at 5 mana would be castable sooner and provides board impact. Formidable Speaker is the weakest option by far.

Playing Undercity Sewers (enters tapped) instead of Overgrown Tomb (can enter untapped for 2 life) means Timmy misses the opportunity to cast Formidable Speaker this turn. With Overgrown Tomb untapped, the available mana would be Hedge Maze (G/U) + Gloomlake Verge (U/B) + Overgrown Tomb (B/G) = 3 mana including 2G, enabling Formidable Speaker which could tutor a key creature like Superior Spider-Man or another threat while developing the board.

Discarded No More Lies (a valuable counterspell) instead of the weakest land in hand. Against an opponent with multiple devastating spells in their deck (Bringer of the Last Gift, Ardyn), having two counterspells available is significantly more valuable than a third land drop when Libby already has three other lands in hand and adequate color sources on board.

Casting Superior Spider-Man before playing Overgrown Tomb from hand. Playing the land first would leave an additional mana available after casting Spider-Man (3 mana up instead of 2), which is relevant for holding up Bitter Triumph or Requiting Hex. Lands should generally be played before spells.

Copying The Unagi of Kyoshi Island provides ward protection and a conditional card draw trigger, but copying Overlord of the Balemurk would trigger its ETB to mill 4 cards and return a powerful creature (like Bringer of the Last Gift or Ardyn) from graveyard to hand, generating immediate card advantage. The Unagi's draw trigger requires the opponent to draw their second card each turn, which is not guaranteed.

Discarding Ardyn, the Usurper as the additional cost for Bitter Triumph targeting their own Superior Spider-Man. While the discard choice itself is defensible (Ardyn costs 5BBB and is extremely hard to cast), the broader play of using Bitter Triumph to destroy your own creature is highly suspect - it's a 2-for-1 against yourself (spending Bitter Triumph + discarding Ardyn) for no clear benefit. There's already an Ardyn in the graveyard, so the second copy could have some marginal graveyard value, but the cost is enormous.

Playing Restless Anchorage (enters tapped) instead of an untapped land like Floodfarm Verge or Island reduces available mana from 3 to 2 this turn. While 2 mana covers No More Lies (WU), having 3 mana would allow holding up Three Steps Ahead's counter mode (1UU) against the opponent's upcoming threats. The opponent has 7 lands that will untap and a graveyard-heavy deck with powerful spells to cast.

Casting Seam Rip before playing a land drop this turn. With Steam Vents, Floodfarm Verge, and Island in hand, Libby should play a land first to maximize available mana. Additionally, the primary threat is Overlord of the Balemurk (MV 5) which Seam Rip cannot exile, so holding up countermagic (No More Lies + Three Steps Ahead) with more mana available would be stronger.

Casting Formidable Speaker before playing Watery Grave is a sequencing error. Playing the land first would give access to more mana this turn and ensure the land drop isn't missed if something unexpected happens. Additionally, Formidable Speaker's ETB lets you discard a card to tutor a creature, but with Rest in Peace on the battlefield exiling all cards that would go to the graveyard, the discard still works mechanically (the card gets exiled instead), but the key issue is that Overlord of the Balemurk's mill and graveyard recursion are completely shut off by Rest in Peace. Speaker could tutor for an answer to Rest in Peace, which is good, but the land should still be played first to maximize available mana.

Tutored for Bringer of the Last Gift while Rest in Peace is on the battlefield, which completely negates Bringer's reanimation ability (sacrificed creatures get exiled, and no creatures exist in graveyards to return). The card becomes an overcosted 8-mana 6/6 flyer with a self-destructive ETB.

Used the more flexible and expensive counterspell (Three Steps Ahead, 3 mana) to counter Consult the Star Charts when No More Lies (2 mana) would have been equally effective since the opponent likely cannot pay the {3} tax with at most 2 untapped lands remaining. This wastes the more versatile spell and leaves less mana open.

Opponent cast Consult the Star Charts with 7 lands, meaning they get to look at 7 cards and pick the best one (or two if kicked). Libby has both No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead available with untapped mana (Island + Hallowed Fountain = WU for No More Lies, or U for Three Steps Ahead's counter mode at 1UU total). Letting a card selection spell resolve against an opponent with Overlord of the Balemurk and Formidable Speaker on board means the opponent likely finds exactly what they need (possibly Bringer of the Last Gift or Sunderflock or another major threat). With Rest in Peace neutering graveyard strategies, the opponent is pivoting to find answers or threats through card selection, and countering this denies them significant card quality. No More Lies would cost the opponent 3 mana they likely can't pay (their lands appear tapped), effectively hard countering it and exiling it.

Rest in Peace is on the opponent's battlefield, which exiles all cards that would go to graveyards instead. Bringer of the Last Gift's enter-the-battlefield ability forces each player to sacrifice all other creatures, then returns creature cards from graveyards to the battlefield — but with Rest in Peace, the sacrificed creatures get exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and there are no creature cards in any graveyard to return. This means casting Bringer of the Last Gift results in sacrificing Formidable Speaker and Overlord of the Balemurk for nothing — a massive self-inflicted board wipe with zero upside. The player loses two important permanents and gets only a 6/6 flyer, while spending 8 mana.

Bringer of the Last Gift is on the stack - an 8-mana 6/6 flyer that, when it enters, forces each player to sacrifice all other creatures then returns all creature cards from graveyards to the battlefield. The opponent has Rest in Peace on Libby's board exiling graveyards, but the sacrifice effect is still devastating. More critically, with Rest in Peace in play, the opponent's graveyard is exiled, so the 'return creatures from graveyard' part helps nobody - BUT the opponent still gets a 6/6 flyer and forces Libby to sacrifice nothing (Libby has no creatures). However, the opponent has Formidable Speaker and Overlord of the Balemurk on the battlefield - Bringer's ETB would force the opponent to sacrifice those too. Wait - actually, let me reconsider. The opponent sacrifices all OTHER creatures (Formidable Speaker, and Overlord of the Balemurk if it's a creature - it was cast with Impending so it's not a creature yet). Then graveyards are exiled by Rest in Peace, so nothing comes back. So the opponent ends up with just a 6/6 flyer and loses Formidable Speaker. Libby has No More Lies (costs WU, needs 3 to pay) and Three Steps Ahead (costs U + 1U to counter). Libby has 4 untapped lands: Island, Hallowed Fountain, Rest in Peace (not a land), Seam Rip (not a land) - actually looking at the battlefield, tapped are: Hallowed Fountain, Meticulous Archive, Restless Anchorage, Floodfarm Verge. Untapped: Island, Hallowed Fountain (second one), and... that's only 2 untapped lands producing W and U. No More Lies costs WU - Libby can cast it with Island (U) + Hallowed Fountain (W). Three Steps Ahead counter mode costs 1UU - needs 3 mana. Libby only has 2 untapped lands. So only No More Lies is castable. A 6/6 flyer is a massive threat that will kill Libby in 3 attacks (Libby is at 16). Libby should counter this. Letting it resolve gives the opponent a dominant board position.

Using Get Lost on Overlord of the Balemurk while Rest in Peace is already on the battlefield neutralizing its graveyard synergies. The Overlord still has time counters remaining before becoming a creature, so it's not an immediate threat. Get Lost gives the opponent two Map tokens, which provide card filtering/exploration value. With counterspells (No More Lies, Three Steps Ahead) in hand, Libby could afford to wait and use Get Lost on a more threatening permanent later.

Letting it resolve risks losing the most important card on Libby's board against this Overlord of the Balemurk / Bringer of the Last Gift deck.

Discarded Harvester of Misery (a castable 5/4 menace for 5 mana) to keep Sunderflock, which costs 9 mana with no Elemental cost reduction available. While Sunderflock's mass bounce is powerful, it requires exactly 9 mana and the opponent has Rest in Peace and Seam Rip (enchantments) that won't be bounced. Harvester provides an immediate castable threat.

More importantly, playing Willowrush Verge would bring Timmy to 9 lands, enabling casting Sunderflock (which costs 9 with no Elementals in play) next turn. Playing Meticulous Archive (enters tapped) instead of Island (enters untapped) when wanting to hold up countermagic (No More Lies + Three Steps Ahead). While surveil 1 provides some deck filtering, Rest in Peace is on the battlefield, meaning any card surveilled to the graveyard gets exiled instead, significantly reducing the value. With Overlord of the Balemurk counting down time counters, maximizing available mana for counterspells is important.

Grok4F Libby declined to counter Day of Judgment while having both No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead available. Rest in Peace is on the battlefield, which means the opponent's graveyard is exiled and their Overlord of the Balemurk's mill/recursion strategy is neutered. However, Restless Anchorage is Libby's primary win condition as a creature land, and Day of Judgment doesn't destroy it (it's not currently a creature). Looking more carefully: Libby has no creatures on board - Seam Rip is an enchantment exiling something, Rest in Peace is an enchantment, and Restless Anchorage is a land. The opponent has Overlord of the Balemurk as a non-creature enchantment (it was cast with Impending, so it still has time counters and isn't a creature yet). So Day of Judgment actually destroys nothing on either side currently. In that case, letting it resolve is correct since it's a wasted spell by the opponent. Wait - let me reconsider. Overlord of the Balemurk with Impending means it's not a creature yet. Libby has no creatures. Day of Judgment would destroy zero creatures. Letting it resolve wastes the opponent's card and preserves Libby's counterspells for actual threats. This is actually the correct play.

Cast Sunderflock before playing a land. With only 8 lands and Sunderflock costing 9 mana (no Elementals to reduce cost), the correct sequence is to play Willowrush Verge first (enters untapped due to controlling Forests/Islands), giving 9 lands to properly cast Sunderflock. Additionally, playing the land first preserves the land drop in case Sunderflock gets countered (opponent has W+U open for No More Lies).

Playing Watery Grave over Willowrush Verge when Timmy already has abundant U/B sources. Watery Grave either costs 2 life (at 12 life against a deck with Restless Anchorage pressure) or enters tapped, while Willowrush Verge enters untapped for free and produces U or G (G enabled by existing Islands). With only Requiting Hex in hand needing B mana they already have plenty of, there's no reason to prioritize Watery Grave.

Cast Aang's Iceberg in precombat main phase with no nonland permanents to exile on opponent's side, while opponent is tapped out at 10 life. This wastes 3 mana that could have been used to activate Restless Anchorage for a 2/3 flying attack, applying pressure and creating a Map token.

Cast Superior Spider-Man before playing Willowrush Verge. Land should be played first for correct sequencing, even though the extra mana isn't needed for this specific spell. Additionally, Superior Spider-Man's Mind Swap ability is completely blanked by the opponent's Rest in Peace (all graveyards are exiled), making it just a vanilla 4/4 - though with only these two cards in hand, casting it is still the best available play.

Cast Get Lost with no meaningful opposing targets on the board. The opponent has only lands in play - no creatures, enchantments, or planeswalkers to destroy. The only valid targets would be Libby's own Rest in Peace or Seam Rip, which is counterproductive and gives the opponent two Map tokens for free.

message: Select a creature, enchantment, or planeswalker
annotation_description: Get Lost is on the stack, almost certainly targeting Rest in Peace, which is the key hate piece shutting down the opponent's entire graveyard-based strategy (Overlord of the Balemurk recursion, etc.). Libby has both No More Lies and Three Steps Ahead in hand with mana available to cast either, but chose not to counter.

Cast Aang's Iceberg when the opponent has no nonland permanents on the battlefield, wasting 3 mana and a card for no meaningful effect. Three Steps Ahead in draw mode would have generated card advantage while still leaving mana to hold up No More Lies.

Grok4F Libby chose to cast Aang's Iceberg (which exiles a nonland permanent — but the opponent has none on the battlefield) instead of No More Lies to counter Three Steps Ahead on the stack. The opponent had only 2 untapped mana remaining after casting Three Steps Ahead, so they couldn't pay the {3} tax from No More Lies, meaning it would have been a hard counter. Instead, Three Steps Ahead resolves (likely drawing 2 cards) and Aang's Iceberg accomplishes nothing.

Naming 'Human' on Cavern of Souls when the deck's most impactful creatures appear to be non-Human types. Overlord of the Balemurk is an Avatar, and Sunderflock (in the card reference) is an Elemental. Against a UW control deck with counterspells, making the biggest threats uncounterable would be more valuable.

Grok4F Libby cast Stock Up (a sorcery costing 2U) during their main phase before playing their Plains land drop. By playing Plains first, they would have had 9 lands available instead of 8, which matters for leaving up countermagic (No More Lies costs WU) after casting their draw spell. With 8 lands and Stock Up costing 3, they have 5 mana remaining - enough for No More Lies. However, if they had played Plains first, they could have cast Consult the Star Charts (kicked for 1U + 1U = 4 mana total) instead with the benefit of looking at 9 cards and getting 2, which would likely be superior to Stock Up's look-at-5-get-2, while still leaving 5 mana open for countermagic. Additionally, the general principle of playing lands before spells avoids information loss.

With no opponent creatures on board, declining to activate Restless Anchorage as a 2/3 flyer to attack for 2 damage misses free pressure. With 8 lands available, activating for {1}{W}{U} still leaves 5 lands untapped - enough to hold up No More Lies ({W}{U}) or Tishana's Tidebinder ({2}{U}) for protection. At 2 life vs 10 life, every point of damage matters to close out the game before the opponent draws threats.

Cast Day of Judgment with zero creatures on the entire battlefield. The spell destroys nothing and is completely wasted. At 2 life with limited cards in hand, throwing away a board wipe that could have been critical later is devastating.

At 2 life with the opponent at 8, Grok4F Libby needs a win condition. Restless Anchorage is a flying creature land that can attack for 2 and create Map tokens - it's the primary way a control deck closes games. With 8 lands already in play, they have more than enough untapped mana to hold up No More Lies (WU), Spell Snare (U), and Tidebinder (2U) even with Restless Anchorage entering tapped. Plains provides redundant mana with no strategic upside.

Casting Tishana's Tidebinder in precombat main phase before playing the Restless Anchorage land. Lands should be played before spells as a general sequencing principle - it's free and keeps options open. Additionally, Tidebinder has flash and could be held up alongside counterspells to react to opponent's plays, which is especially relevant at 2 life where every decision matters.

At 2 life with Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2 flash) on the stack, activating Restless Anchorage now makes it a creature only until end of THIS turn - it won't be available as a blocker during the opponent's next combat. Meanwhile, No More Lies would either counter the Tidebinder (if opponent can't pay 3) or at minimum tax 3 mana from the opponent. Letting a 3/2 resolve when at 2 life without attempting to counter it is potentially game-losing.

GPT4om Timmy used Awaken the Honored Dead's Chapter I destroy ability to target itself, completely wasting the card for no effect. The opponent is at 2 life and has Rest in Peace (which shuts down graveyard strategies), Seam Rip (which is exiling one of Timmy's permanents), and Tishana's Tidebinder on the battlefield. Any of these would have been a meaningful target. Rest in Peace is particularly devastating as it exiles all cards that would go to graveyards, neutering Timmy's entire game plan. Tishana's Tidebinder is a 3/2 creature that could block or attack. Seam Rip is exiling something. Instead, Timmy destroyed their own saga for zero value.

Grok4F Libby is at 2 life and their opponent cast Bitter Triumph targeting Tishana's Tidebinder. Libby has Spell Snare in hand, which counters spells with mana value 2 — Bitter Triumph costs {1}{B} and has mana value 2, making it a valid target. Libby also has No More Lies available. By not countering Bitter Triumph, Libby loses Tishana's Tidebinder, which was likely locking down something important (possibly Overlord of the Balemurk). At 2 life with the opponent also at 2, losing a key creature and potentially unlocking an opponent's threat is devastating. Either Spell Snare (free, costs only {U}) or No More Lies would have saved the Tidebinder.

At 2 life each with no opponent creatures on board, Restless Anchorage would provide a lethal attacker next turn (2/3 flyer for {1}{W}{U}) while still allowing countermagic backup. Cori Mountain Monastery provides red mana that doesn't support any cards in hand and delays the win condition by a turn.

Cast Day of Judgment with zero creatures on either side of the battlefield, accomplishing nothing and wasting a card. The opponent is at 2 life with no creatures, and Restless Anchorage was available as a land drop that becomes a 2/3 flyer — which would attack for lethal next turn.

At 2 life each in a control mirror with only counterspells in hand, Libby declined to play Restless Anchorage - a creature land that serves as a win condition. Both players are at 2 life, and Restless Anchorage can become a 2/3 flyer to attack for lethal. Since it enters tapped, playing it in postcombat main has zero downside - it doesn't reduce available mana for counterspells this turn.

Jeskai Revelation is on the stack and can deal 4 damage to Libby who is at 2 life. Not countering it with No More Lies allows a lethal spell to resolve. Even if the opponent could pay the {3} tax, Libby should attempt the counter since dying is the alternative.
